194	    62	## Score structure
195	    63	
196	    64	100 BPM, F major, under the voice. Opening F → B♭; the gate a pizzicato walk under the line; a harp sweep as the lid opens; a stuck pizzicato stab and a held cello D while the line waits; piano sixteenths for the time-lapse and a low Dm on 6:54; one second of score backwards for the rewind and a glockenspiel run as the seats light; a rising vibraphone F A C F at the second gate; one six-note vibraphone chord per wave in the weave with pizzicato and shaker under it; F with glockenspiel on 3:36; B♭ → Gm under the bars and C on the bracket; F/A under the 72 passengers, Dm under the callback, a long F under the sign-off. A soft cello root sustains under every shot and overlaps each cut. The music ducks 16 dB under the narration and lifts between lines. Mix: −16.0 LUFS integrated, true peak −2.1 dBFS before mux (English: −16.0 / −2.3).

237	     1	# 2.5D Pixel Art — Style Prompt
238	     2	
239	     3	> Hand-made pixel sprites standing like paper cut-outs inside a lit, fogged, fully 3D diorama, shot from a high three-quarter angle through a tilt-shift lens: a toy world where every lamp throws a real shadow.
240	     4	> References (grammar only): *Octopath Traveler* (Square Enix × Acquire, 2018) and its sequel (2023), the games that defined the HD-2D look. Learn the grammar: sprite-in-diorama, high 3/4 camera, tilt-shift focus band, point lights with shadows, heavy bloom and vignette, framed dialogue box. Never use their characters, places, logos, UI ornaments or music, and never name them in the film.
241	     5	> Name: this style was formerly called "HD-2D", Square Enix's term (and trademark) for that look; the library uses the term only to describe the look. This style and its demo have no connection to Square Enix and are not endorsed by it. Don't use "HD-2D" as a title or brand in a film.
242	     6	
243	     7	## 1. Essence, and what it is not
244	     8	
245	     9	A **3D miniature set** of boxes and cylinders wrapped in **pixel-art textures**, populated by **flat 2D pixel sprites that receive light and cast shadows**, seen from a **high, far camera** through a **tilt-shift band** so the world reads as a tabletop model. **Light is the subject**: practicals throw sprite shadows across the floor; shafts, fog, dust or rain hang in the air; strong bloom, heavy vignette. On top, a small **RPG UI**: chapter card, framed dialogue box with typewriter text, serif subtitles.
246	    10	
247	    11	The key contrast: characters stay **flat, low-res and stepped** while camera, light, particles and focus move smoothly every frame.
248	    12	
249	    13	Not a voxel game (no cubic characters), not a flat 2D pixel RPG (the set is real 3D with real light), not a tilt-shift photo of a real miniature (textures are pixels, not materials).
250	    14	
251	    15	## 2. Materials & rendering
252	    16	
253	    17	- **Constant texel density**: surfaces drawn per pixel on small canvases, `NearestFilter`, world-space UVs at one density (e.g. 24 px/m); sprites on a similar scale (a character ~30–60 px tall).
254	    18	- **Colour from ramps**: 3–6 swatches picked by brightness through a narrow 4×4 Bayer dither. Sprites get a 1 px *selout* outline (neighbour colour darkened toward the ink).
255	    19	- **Boxes and cylinders** for buildings, floors, rock; **billboards** (instanced) for foliage, distant props, ridges. Windows are emissive pixel panes; fire is a pixel atlas stepping at ~10 fps; water a shader with quantized ripples and light columns toward the camera.
256	    20	- **Light rig per set**: one dim shadow-casting key, a hemisphere fill, **practical point lights** with shadows (lamps, fires, windows, screens), and a **front fill** ~2 m before the hero (a billboard lit from behind stays black). An additive glow sprite on every source gives bloom something to grab.
257	    21	- **Post chain, at render time**: supersampled render → physical DOF with tilt-shift in the same signed circle of confusion (above the band = far, below = near; far never bleeds over a sharp foreground) → bloom → vignette/grade → filmic tone map. No film grain.
258	    22	
259	    23	## 3. Colour logic
260	    24	
261	    25	- **Two temperatures**: one large ambient key (cold, or pale, or dusty) against small warm or saturated practicals. The practicals carry the story; the ambient carries the mood.
262	    26	- The darkest value is a warm ink, never pure black; the brightest is the light source itself, bloomed.
263	    27	- Each set owns one fog colour and one light key, so a cut to a new place reads instantly.
264	    28	- The hero wears the one saturated costume colour that no set uses, so the tiny sprite is findable in a wide.
265	    29	- UI is one metal (gold, silver, copper) plus one paper white over a dark translucent plate.
266	    30	- Examples: night canal town (blue fog, amber windows); autumn market at dusk (violet sky, pink paper lanterns); snowy mine at noon (grey-white daylight, green mineral glow).
267	    31	
268	    32	## 4. Type & subtitles
269	    33	
270	    34	- An inscriptional capital serif (Cinzel, wide tracking) for chapter labels and titles; an old-style serif (Cormorant, Cormorant Garamond italic) for subtitles, dialogue, taglines. All OFL.
271	    35	- **Narration subtitles**: italic serif ~46–54 px, centred low on a soft dark gradient band, one line per voice clip, in ~0.35 s before the voice.
272	    36	- **On-screen speech gets a dialogue box**, not a subtitle: dark plate, thin metal border, corner ornaments, name plate on its top edge, text **typed over ~90 % of the voice**, blinking caret, soft chime on entry.
273	    37	- Chapter cards and a title card belong to the grammar. Hold ≥ max(1.8 s, speech + 0.6 s). Export the `.srt` from the data that drives the overlay.
274	    38	
275	    39	## 5. Motion quality
276	    40	
277	    41	- **Sprites step, everything else glides.** Walk cycles 4 frames at 6–10 fps, idles alternate two frames at ~1–2 Hz, blinks every few seconds, pose changes are instant cuts between drawings. Camera, lights, particles, beams and focus update every output frame (60 fps).
278	    42	- **Poses are data**: a parameter object per drawing; a new pose is a new table entry.
279	    43	- **Lights breathe**: every flame flickers (a few summed sines, about ±20 %). A light's level is one value that drives the sprite drawing, the point light (intensity ∝ level^~1.3), the glow opacity and its scale together.
280	    44	- **Weather is procedural**: slanted rain streaks; lightning as a scripted flash curve (strike, dip, re-strike, decay) lifting sky, fill and exposure together.
281	    45	- The world never shakes except for impact; the set never moves, only the camera and what lives in it.
282	    46	
283	    47	## 6. Camera grammar
284	    48	
285	    49	A vocabulary, not a route. Opening and ending come from the topic. Always look **down** on the world (never at eye level); every path is a monotone spline of a few keys, no overshoot; focus is recomputed every frame from camera to the subject.
286	    50	
287	    51	| Move | Expresses | Can serve |
288	    52	|---|---|---|
289	    53	| Very high, very far, slow push; band on one tiny subject | Preciousness, a whole place as a map | where we are; scale; a landmark |
290	    54	| Medium-high 3/4, near-static drift | Two figures on one stage | a conversation; a handover; a choice |
291	    55	| Lateral tracking, camera leading slightly, foreground passing blurred | A path through a world | travel; a process with steps; a commute |
292	    56	| Dive low and close while a figure kneels or stops | The toy world suddenly personal | exhaustion; care; a secret |
293	    57	| Rising pull-back, focus handed from figure to object | The act spreads outward | consequence; a system switching on |
294	    58	| Orbit half-way round a building or prop | An object seen from all sides | a workshop; a machine; a monument |
295	    59	| Top-down, straight overhead, tilt band as a strip | A board game, a plan | routes; a schedule; a queue |
296	    60	| Rack focus between two depths in a locked frame | Attention changing hands | a memory; someone watching; before/after |
297	    61	| Return to an earlier framing, changed | The rhyme shows what changed | aftermath; growth; a season later |
298	    62	
299	    63	Framing: characters ~1/12–1/8 of frame height; the sharp band follows the subject's projected height (clamped ~.2–.8 of screen); with no character, use a fixed band height per shot. Transitions: short fades to black or cuts between sets; no wipes, no 3D spins.
300	    64	
301	    65	## 7. Sound palette
302	    66	
303	    67	- **Music**: chamber-fantasy or cinematic colours (harp, celesta, strings, horns, low choir, timpani) or small folk instruments (lute, recorder, hand drum). Either one piece whose own arc matches the story, **cut inside it** at downbeats, or an original score; a downbeat can land on the frame of a visual event.
304	    68	- **Silence as a tool**: a hard stop into a reverb tail, a pad alone, or one heartbeat when the light nearly dies; a short breath (< 1 s) when something fails.

320	    84	## 9. Pitfalls of the medium
321	    85	
322	    86	- **Checkerboard everywhere** → the dither band is too wide (≈ .22 on sprites, ≈ .45 on textures).
323	    87	- **A light burns out the sprite that holds it** → move the light ~0.45 m toward the camera; cap sprite lighting in the shader (`min(outgoingLight, diffuse * 1.35 + emissive)`).
324	    88	- **Lights behind a billboard don't light it** (front normal only) → always the front fill.
325	    89	- **Cylinder beams facing the camera give NaN** that bloom spreads into black blocks → billboard beam cards that fade toward the lens, glow sprite takes over.
326	    90	- **Dark scenes unreadable** → lift environment mid-tones ~×2–2.5 outside the one beat that must go dark.
327	    91	- **Distant glows hidden by fog** → `depthTest = false`, higher `renderOrder`.
328	    92	- **Tilt-shift with no character to track** → fixed band height per shot. **Tilt as a separate blur pass** breaks occlusion → fold it into the DOF's signed CoC.
329	    93	- **Node render scripts may not exit** after `done` (server keep-alive) → `process.exit(0)`; the file is complete once `done` prints.
330	    94

392	    46	## Palette & props
393	    47	
394	    48	The demo is a night film: cold blue against warm amber fire, strong bloom, heavy vignette.
395	    49	
396	    50	**Resolution & pixels.** Scene textures are drawn per pixel on small canvases (`PX` class, `px.js`) and uploaded with `NearestFilter`; world-space UVs (`worldUV`, `kit.js`) keep **24 px/m** on every surface. Characters are 34×50 px frames at `SPX = 1/30` m per pixel (≈1.67 m tall). Colour comes from **ramps** (3–6 swatches) chosen by brightness with a 4×4 Bayer dither; the dither band `dz` must be narrow: **.22 for characters, .45 for textures** (wider = checkerboard noise everywhere). Sprites get an automatic 1 px **selout** outline (`PX.outline(.3)`: transparent pixels next to the sprite become the neighbour colour darkened toward `#16 0e 1e`).
397	    51	
398	    52	**Palette (night).** Sky `#050818 → #101d3e → #2c4262` (horizon), fog `#16223a` (harbour) / `#152a48` (forest) / `#1c2334` (storm), moon light `#8fa8e0`, hemisphere `#3a4c7a / #0a0a12`. Fire and windows `#ff9d4a`, `#ffae55`, `#ff8c3a`, lantern `#ffb050`, lighthouse `#fff0c8`. Cool character fill `#9fb2e8`. Hero cloak ramp `#2e0b14 … #c9503f` (crimson), scarf gold `#b08424`; keeper coat navy `#10131f … #5a6c98`, beard greys. Ink `#1a1016`.
399	    53	
400	    54	**Materials.** Boxes and cylinders only: houses with plaster + timber beams (`plaster`), shingle roofs (`shingles`), planks with nail dots (`woodPlanks`), Worley cobbles (`cobbles`), layered rock (`rock`), bark/canopy/fern/grass/mushroom sprites (`forest_art.js`). Foliage, grass, ferns, mushrooms, distant ships and ridges are **billboards** (instanced where many). Windows are emissive pixel panes (`windowMat`, emissive 2.2). Fire is a 6-frame pixel atlas billboard at 10 fps (`fire`). Sea is a custom shader: quantized pixel ripples, crest bands, light reflection columns stretched toward the camera, sparkle glints.
401	    55	
402	    56	**Light rig per set.** One dim shadow-casting moon (DirectionalLight 1.1–1.2, 2048 map) + hemisphere fill + **practical point lights** (windows 8, street lamps 12–14, brazier 16 with shadows, lantern 2.6–14 with shadows) + a **cool front fill** (`#9fb2e8`/`#8fa6e0`, 1.2–1.8, range 6–8 m) placed ~2 m in front of the hero. Additive `glow` sprites sit on every light source so bloom has something to grab.
403	    57	
404	    58	**Post chain** (`post_ts.js`, `makePost(renderer, scene, camera, 1920, 1080, { ssaa: 2 })`): render at 2× (3840×2160 internal) with MSAA → physical DOF (CoC = `aper × (1/focus − 1/z)` px, 96-tap spiral gather, far samples cannot bleed over a sharp foreground) **+ tilt-shift** → UnrealBloom (strength .55, radius .75, threshold .85) → vignette/grade (amt .62, warm .1, contrast .2, sat 1.05) → ACES filmic, exposure 1.15. Tilt-shift cut adds: `tiltAmt 17`, band half-width `tiltW .075`, feather `tiltF .3` (fractions of screen height), `maxCoc ≥ 24`, saturation ×1.16, contrast .28.
405	    59	
406	    60	**Type.** Cinzel 500/700 (chapter label, title), Cormorant Garamond italic 500 (subtitles, tagline), Cormorant 500/600 (dialogue text, name plate). Gold `#d8c28e / #e2c989 / #c9a863`, parchment white `#f3ead6 / #f6f0e2`.
407	    61	
408	    62	Motion as built:
409	    63	
410	    64	- **Sprites step, everything else glides.** Walk cycles use 4 frames at 6–10 fps (`['w0','w1','w2','w3'][Math.floor(t*9)%4]`), idles alternate two frames at ~1.4 Hz, blinks every few seconds, poses swap instantly (`upE → up → idle`). Camera, lights, particles, beams and focus update every frame at 60 fps.
411	    65	- **Poses are data**: a frame is a parameter object (`{ step, arm:'low'|'fwd'|'up'|'hug'|'pour', kneel, lit, bob, hem, scarf, blink, closed, look }`) drawn by `drawWren` / `drawKeeper`. Add a pose by adding a table entry (or pass `extra` to `makeChar`).
412	    66	- **The light breathes**: `flick(t, seed)` (three summed sines, ±20 %) on every flame; the lantern's `lit` value (0–1) redraws the flame size in the sprite *and* drives the point light (`intensity ∝ lit^1.3`), glow opacity and scale.
413	    67	- **Events are timestamps** in `story.js` `T` (lighthouse flicker 11.5 → out 12.35, taper 16.2, gust 40.6, dim 41.3, dark 42.0, relight 45.6, stand 47.6, pour 52.6, ignite 53.5, beams 54.4, ships 59.2). Scenes blend with `ss(seg(t,a,b))`.
414	    68	- **Signature beats:** lighthouse flickers twice and dies; brazier taper lights the lantern and both sprites' shadows jump onto the planks; the gust shrinks the flame to an ember (sprite `lit .27`), world goes almost black, then the flame re-grows; the lens ignites with an exposure burst (`exp(-(t-53.5)/.22)`) and two beam cards start sweeping; ships' lamps pop on one every 0.7 s and drift toward the harbour.
415	    69	- **Weather is procedural**: rain = wind-slanted line segments (`rain`), lightning = a scripted flash curve (`flash(t)`: 150 ms strike, dip, 60 ms re-strike, exp decay) that boosts hemisphere, a "bolt" light, sky, clouds, sea and exposure together.

491	   145	Pitfalls, with the demo's props and numbers:
492	   146	
493	   147	- **Checkerboard everywhere**: a wide dither band on ramps. Keep `dz` ≈ .22 on sprites, ≈ .45 on textures.
494	   148	- **The lantern blows out the sprite**: a point light sitting on the billboard plane saturates it. Put the light **0.42–0.45 m from the lantern toward the camera** (`lp + toCam * .45`), and in the forest cap sprite lighting in the shader (`outgoingLight = min(outgoingLight, diffuseColor.rgb * 1.35 + emissive)` via `onBeforeCompile`).
495	   149	- **Lights behind a billboard don't light it** (it only has a front normal). Always add a cool front fill light ~2 m in front of the hero.
496	   150	- **Cylinder light beams facing the camera produce NaN**; bloom spreads them into large black blocks. Use `beamCard` (an axis-aligned billboard strip that fades as it turns toward the camera) and let the glow sprite take over (`face` factor enlarges the lighthouse glow).
497	   151	- **Sea reflection column division by zero**: clamp the width with `max(.35, …)`.
498	   152	- **Storm too dark to read.** Add a "readability" fill outside the story-dark beat: hemisphere +1.0, sun +1.3, sky +.35 (the `ext` term in `cliff.js`), i.e. roughly ×2–2.5 on environment mid-tones, and let it drop to nothing only during the flame-almost-out beat.
499	   153	- **Distant ship glows hidden by fog/geometry**: `depthTest = false` + `renderOrder 5` on those glow sprites.
500	   154	- **Tilt-shift on shots with no character**: the tracker has nothing to follow; use fixed band heights per shot (`TILT_C`).
501	   155	- **Tilt-shift and occlusion**: the tilt blur is folded into the same signed CoC as depth DOF (above the band = far, below = near) so the gather keeps the "far can't bleed over sharp near" rule; don't add it as a separate blur pass.
502	   156	- **Near-identical frames diverge around a flash**: the ignition burst decays with a 0.22 s time constant, so a still at 53.8 s differs visibly from the neighbouring 60 fps frame. That is expected, not a bug.
503	   157	- **Node render scripts may not exit** after `done` because the static server keeps connections alive (`demo/tools/render_range.mjs` ends with `process.exit(0)` for that reason). The output file is complete once `done` is printed.
504	   158	
505	   159	## Engine reference
506	   160	
507	   161	### Page contract (`main.js`)
508	   162	`window.render(t)` picks the shot (`shotAt(t)`), maps it to a set (`SET_OF`), points the DOF pass at that set's scene, resets post defaults (bloom .55/.85, exposure 1.15, warm .1, sat 1.05, vignette .62), calls `set.update(t, shot, camera, post, renderer)`, applies tilt-shift if `?tilt`, renders the composer, then draws the overlay (`drawOverlay(t, shot)`). One `PerspectiveCamera(32, 16/9, .3, 2000)` is shared by all sets; each set sets fov/position/lookAt every frame.
509	   163	
510	   164	### Modules and key functions
511	   165	| Module | Function | What / key params |
512	   166	|---|---|---|
513	   167	| `px.js` | `new PX(w,h)` | `.set/.get/.rect/.fill(f)/.ellipse/.poly/.line/.outline(k,tint)/.done()` → canvas |
514	   168	| | `ramp(cols, dz=.45)` | `(v,x,y) → rgb` with Bayer dither; `dz` = dither band width |
515	   169	| | `texOf(canvas, {repeat, mip, linear})` | NearestFilter texture |
516	   170	| | `woodPlanks / cobbles / rock / plaster / shingles / ground(w,h,o)` | procedural surface canvases (`seed`, `cols`, `pw`, `len`, `cell`, `beams`, `snow`) |
517	   171	| | `billboard(tex, wM, hM, {ax, ay, em, emCol, emI, shadow, receive})` | upright lit sprite plane (Lambert + alphaTest .5) with custom depth/distance materials so it casts cut-out shadows |
518	   172	| | `glow(col, size, i)` · `blob(r, a)` · `radialTex` | additive halo sprite · ground contact shadow |
519	   173	| `kit.js` | `worldUV(geo, tile)` · `mat(canvas, o)` · `mesh(geo, m)` · `box(w,h,d,m)` | planar UVs by normal so texel density is constant (`tile = canvas.width / 24` m) |
520	   174	| | `mats()` | cached `plank, plankDark, beam, wall, wall2, wall3, roof, roof2, roof3` |
521	   175	| | `house({x,z,w,d,h,wall,roof,door,windows,upper,side,chimney,ry})` | timber house with emissive windows (`g.userData.windows`) |
522	   176	| | `crate(s)` · `barrel(r,h)` · `fire(size,{seed,i})` · `windowQuad` · `ridge(wM,hM,col,seed)` | props; `fire.userData.update(t, cam, scale)` |
523	   177	| `fx.js` | `sky({top,mid,hor,moonDir,moonCol})` → `{mesh,u}` | gradient dome + moon halo; `u.k` = brightness |
524	   178	| | `stars(n, seed)` · `sea(size,{ppm,deep,shallow,crest})` → `{mesh,u,setLights([{p,c,i}])}` | per frame set `u.t`, `u.camPos`, fog uniforms, `u.bright`, `u.calm` |

526	   180	| | `rain(n, box, {speed,len,opacity})` · `.userData.update(t, [windX,0])` | slanted streaks |
527	   181	| | `beamCard(len, w0, w1, col, {k, fall})` · `.userData.aim(origin, dir, cam)` → side factor | light beam that never shows its edge |
528	   182	| | `flick(t, seed)` | flame flicker multiplier ≈ 1 ± .2 |
529	   183	| `chars.js` | `makeChar('wren'|'keeper', extraPoses)` → `{root, mesh, frame(name), face(cam, flip), lanternPos(name, flip)}` | 34×50 px atlas + emissive atlas (lantern glass); `root.userData.char` is what the tilt tracker looks for |
530	   184	| `post_ts.js` | `makePost(renderer, scene, cam, w, h, {ssaa, ao})` → `{composer, dof, bloom, vig}` | `dof.focus` (m), `dof.aper` (px·m), `dof.maxCoc` (px), `dof.tiltAmt/tiltC/tiltW/tiltF`; `vig.uniforms.amt/warm/sat/contrast/fade` |
531	   185	| `ui.js` | `drawOverlay(t, shot)` · `overlayReady()` | reads `story.js` `VO` and `voices/dur.json` |
532	   186	| `/core/lib.js` | `track(keys)` · `monotone` · `seg` · `ss` · `eio` · `eo` · `lerp` · `clamp` | camera paths and easing |
533	   187	
534	   188	### Minimal new set
535	   189	```js
536	   190	// myset.js — a lantern-lit alley; register in main.js: sets.alley = buildAlley(); SET_OF.alley = 'alley'; add { id:'alley', a, b } to story.js SHOTS
537	   191	import * as THREE from 'three';
538	   192	import { cobbles, glow } from './px.js';
539	   193	import { mat, mesh, house } from './kit.js';
540	   194	import { sky, particles, flick } from './fx.js';
541	   195	import { makeChar } from './chars.js';
542	   196	import { track, seg, ss } from '/core/lib.js';
543	   197	
544	   198	export function buildAlley() {
545	   199	  const scene = new THREE.Scene(); scene.fog = new THREE.FogExp2('#16223a', .03);
546	   200	  const SK = sky(); scene.add(SK.mesh);
547	   201	  const moon = new THREE.DirectionalLight('#8fa8e0', 1.1); moon.position.set(-20, 30, -20); moon.castShadow = true; moon.shadow.mapSize.set(2048, 2048);
548	   202	  scene.add(moon, new THREE.HemisphereLight('#3a4c7a', '#0a0a12', .9));
549	   203	  scene.add(mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(30, .4, 12).translate(0, -.2, 0), mat(cobbles(96, 96))));
550	   204	  scene.add(house({ x: -4, z: -5, w: 6, d: 5, h: 4.5, door: 1.2 }), house({ x: 4, z: -5, w: 5, d: 5, h: 5, wall: 'wall3', roof: 'roof2' }));
551	   205	  const hero = makeChar('wren'); scene.add(hero.root);
552	   206	  const lamp = new THREE.PointLight('#ffb050', 3, 10, 2); lamp.castShadow = true; lamp.shadow.bias = -.004; scene.add(lamp);
553	   207	  const halo = glow('#ffc070', 1.1, 1.2); scene.add(halo);
554	   208	  const fill = new THREE.PointLight('#9fb2e8', 1.5, 7, 2); scene.add(fill);                 // cool front fill: never skip
555	   209	  const dust = particles(80, (i, t, o) => { o.x = (i * 7.3 % 20) - 10 + t * .1; o.y = (i * 3.1 % 4); o.z = (i * 5.7 % 6) - 3; o.a = .3; o.s = .05; o.r = .7; o.g = .8; o.b = 1; }, { soft: 1 });
556	   210	  scene.add(dust);
557	   211	  const camP = track([[0, [-2, 5.5, 10]], [8, [2, 5, 9]]]), camL = track([[0, [-1, .8, 0]], [8, [2, .8, 0]]]);
558	   212	
559	   213	  function update(t, shot, cam, post) {
560	   214	    const lt = t - shot.a;
561	   215	    cam.position.set(...camP(lt)); cam.fov = 30; cam.updateProjectionMatrix(); cam.lookAt(...camL(lt));
562	   216	    const x = -3 + ss(seg(lt, .5, 7.5)) * 6, walking = lt > .5 && lt < 7.5;
563	   217	    hero.root.position.set(x, 0, 0); hero.frame(walking ? ['w0', 'w1', 'w2', 'w3'][Math.floor(t * 9) % 4] : 'idle0'); hero.face(cam);
564	   218	    const lp = hero.lanternPos('w0'), toCam = cam.position.clone().sub(lp).setY(0).normalize();
565	   219	    lamp.position.copy(lp).addScaledVector(toCam, .45); lamp.intensity = 2.6 * flick(t, 3); halo.position.copy(lp);   // light 0.45 m toward the lens

content.text:
## Toy and miniature 3D styles: research report

I read STYLE.md, DEMO.md and style.json for all six styles, plus the main demo JS. All refs below are relative to `C:\Users\dripp\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\732d969d39f77772\fc08cf29-4653-41a6-8898-85fde8451ca6\scratchpad\ext_opuscar\repo\styles\`.

### 1. What makes each look good

**brick-toy** (the closest match to your box characters)
- **Lighting** (`brick-toy/demo/set.js:28-37`):
  - Key: warm-white directional light `#fff4e8` at 3.0, upper left, 4096 shadow map. Its shadow frustum is shrunk to each shot (span 32 for close shots, 95 for wides) to keep shadows sharp (`main.js:165-168`).
  - Fill: cool `#cfe0ff` at 0.45.
  - Three rectangular softboxes give the plastic its highlights: key 6 front-left, cool rim 9 behind, one over the finale set.
  - Environment kept low at 0.45 for contrast (STYLE.md:21).
- **AO is mandatory.** GTAO radius about 3.5 studs, amount 0.9 (`main.js:19`). The doc says "Without it bricks look pasted on" (STYLE.md:22).
- **Materials:** clearcoat 0.85 with clearcoat roughness 0.07. A roughness map adds fingerprints and scratches (base 0.17, up to 0.65). Edges are bevelled (radius 0.045–0.06) so they catch a highlight (STYLE.md:18-19; `bricks.js:36`). The big baseplate is matte (clearcoat 0.12) (`set.js:92`).
- **Camera:** fov 24–46 (about 25–50 mm). Real depth of field, with aperture scaled to shot size: about 1100 for macro, 500–700 for close-ups, 800 for mediums, 400 for the wide (DEMO.md:28; `main.js:129-161`). Focus is always on the head or the brick being placed.
- **Post:** supersample 2×, Neutral tone mapping, vignette 0.36, contrast +0.26, saturation ×1.1, cool grade (warm −0.35), very little bloom (0.14) (`main.js:13-21`).
- **Characters:** a rigid joint rig built from bricks (`actors.js`). Walk is legs ±0.55 rad, arms at 0.6× that, a bob of |cos|·0.18 (`actors.js:121-124`). Blink every 37 animation frames, about every 3 s (`main.js:65`). Poses are big and held: a hop of about 0.9, arms flung up for alarm, head bowed for sadness (`main.js:73-112`).
- **Timing:** characters animate at 12 fps; the camera moves at 24 fps.
- **Colour:** saturated toys against a muted real-world desk.

**lowpoly-island**
- **Lighting and materials:** flat shading, roughness about 0.9, no textures. Each tile's lightness is jittered ±4% (STYLE.md:16). Lights are a hemisphere at 1.1 and a sun `#fff6e8` at 2.6 (`main.js:26-27`).
- **Post** (DEMO.md:54): GTAO radius 0.7, then a depth-to-gradient-sky haze, a light tilt-shift of 3 px at the frame edges, bloom 0.22 by day and 0.5 at night, saturation 1.04–1.1, Neutral tone mapping, no grain.
- **How things arrive** (DEMO.md:53; `world.js:391-396`):
  - Rise: 0.5 s cubic ease, then overshoot `sin(13s)·e^(−7s)·0.18`.
  - Drop: falls in 0.22 s, bounces `|sin(15s)|·e^(−9s)·0.22`, then squashes `1−0.16e^(−12s)cos(26s)` with volume preserved.
  - Pop: scale `1−e^(−9s)cos(17s)`, about 25% overshoot.
- **Life:** windmills, smoke and gulls keep moving; boats bob on the same wave as the sea.
- **Colour:** time of day is a set of keyframed colours (`story.js:51-62`).

**memphis-diorama**
- **Shading:** three tones per face, from ×1 down to ×0.5–0.95. Shadows are hard and tinted purple, base × (0.70, 0.58, 0.90), with halftone dots inside them. A 2 px indigo outline `#25214A` is drawn as a post pass (STYLE.md:18-21).
- **Colour:** 5–7 saturated hues plus 2–3 pastels, clustered by area (STYLE.md:31-32).
- **Motion:** 60 fps and everything eases. Each object has its own phase, so nothing moves in step. A change of state is announced by a squash followed by a spring (STYLE.md:52-56).
- **Camera:** fov 30, one slow orbit that eases to 0.3× speed after 18 s (DEMO.md:25).
- **Explicitly excluded:** depth of field, bloom and motion blur (STYLE.md:25).

**white-model**
- **Materials and lights:** matte white `#F3F3F1`, roughness 0.88. One soft key light plus a neutral studio environment, and AO only on close shots (STYLE.md:18-19).
- **Projected colour:** `colour × (0.42 + 0.58·N·L)`, so data colour is light that falls on the model, not paint.
- **Post:** depth of field stronger on close shots, bloom 0.32 with threshold 0.85, vignette 0.42, light grain (`studio.js:25-27`).
- **Camera:** one continuous take that changes speed and never stops dead (STYLE.md:47).

**isometric-picture-book**
- **Look:** flat colour in three tones that shade toward warm umber, "never toward grey or violet" (STYLE.md:32).
- **Accent colour:** one accent, used only where the rule is being explained.
- **Characters:** faceless figures seen from behind, walking at 1.5 m/s.
- **Camera:** each shot is a slow drift or push of about 6–8% zoom (`film.js:173-183`, e.g. k 58→62).
- **Motion:** 30 fps, and "Everything eases; nothing pops" (STYLE.md:51).

**hd-2d**
- **Lighting:** practical point lights with shadows, plus a cool front fill about 2 m in front of the hero, because a billboard lit from behind stays black (STYLE.md:20).
- **Colour:** two temperatures, a cold ambient against warm practicals. The darkest value is a warm ink, never black. The hero wears the one saturated colour no set uses (STYLE.md:25-28).
- **Post** (DEMO.md:58):
  - 2× supersampling and real depth of field, with tilt-shift folded into the same blur.
  - Bloom 0.55 (radius 0.75, threshold 0.85).
  - Vignette 0.62, ACES tone mapping, exposure 1.15, no grain.
- **Sprite animation:** this is the closest analogue to your 32×32 faces. Sprites step: a 4-frame walk at 6–10 fps, a two-frame idle at about 1.4 Hz, a blink every few seconds, and instant pose swaps. Camera, lights and particles stay smooth at 60 fps (DEMO.md:64; `chars.js:144-156`).
- **Lights breathe:** ±20% flicker on every flame.

### 2. Story and pacing rules
- **Shot length:**
  - lowpoly-island: about 12 shots in 53 s, every cut on a 2.5 s bar (`story.js:65-78`).
  - brick-toy: cuts every bar (about 1.67 s) only in the building montage, then 3.5–5 s shots for the emotional beats (`story.js:51-56`).
  - isometric-picture-book: one shot per narration line, 2.6–6.7 s (DEMO.md:21-36).
  - hd-2d: 6 sets in 76 s, about 10 s each.
  - memphis-diorama and white-model: a single continuous take.

  - "Track it and keep its destination in frame" (brick-toy STYLE.md:93).
  - A mover should "move across the frame, not toward the lens" (lowpoly-island DEMO.md:27).

### 3. Failure modes the docs warn about (quoted)
- **brick-toy:**
  - "Flat, slightly jagged first renders: even light, no AO, single-sample rendering, stepped camera" (STYLE.md:91). This is close to your PS1 symptoms.
  - "Stepping the camera too reads as judder, not charm" (STYLE.md:43).
  - "Tungsten HDRI → orange whites" (STYLE.md:89).
  - "A fast-rising or fast-moving object becomes a dot on a blank wall" (STYLE.md:93).
- **lowpoly-island:** "Camera too close for its frustum → the frame bottom shows below the sea" (STYLE.md:92). "Two pieces landing in one grid slot muddy the melody" (STYLE.md:93). "grain 0 (flat colour shimmers with grain)" (STYLE.md:73).
- **memphis-diorama:**
  - "Code-made faces, gestures… always look stiff" (STYLE.md:14).

  - "A long take drifts until the subject leaves the frame" (STYLE.md:109).
- **isometric-picture-book:** "dirty shadows are the fastest way to lose this look" (STYLE.md:32). "A path that zigzags… reads as noise" (STYLE.md:88). Movement faster than about 6 m/s "reads as teleporting" (STYLE.md:94).
- **hd-2d:**

  - "Dark scenes unreadable → lift environment mid-tones ~×2–2.5" (STYLE.md:90).
  - "Checkerboard everywhere → the dither band is too wide" (STYLE.md:86).
- **white-model:** "Warm HDRIs turn the white model beige" (STYLE.md:88). "GTAO on wide grazing views produces wedge-shaped dark bands" (STYLE.md:89).

### 4. The 10 most transferable techniques, ranked by impact
1. **Replace flat lighting with a toy-photography rig.** Use a warm key with crisp shadows (about 3.0, `#fff4e8`), a cool fill (about 0.45, `#cfe0ff`), large area-light softboxes (key 6 front, cool rim 9 behind), and keep the world light low (about 0.45). Fit the shadow area to each shot. (brick-toy `set.js:28-37`)
2. **Turn on ambient occlusion every time.** GTAO at a radius of a few character-units, amount about 0.9, so seams and contact points darken and objects stop looking "pasted on". (brick-toy STYLE.md:22; lowpoly-island DEMO.md:54)
3. **Cut far less, and cut on the music.** Plan one action per shot of about 2.5–5 s, cut on bars, and give each narration line its own shot. Make every shot a slow move (about 6–8% push or a slow orbit) instead of a static shot cut short. (lowpoly-island `story.js:65`; isometric-picture-book DEMO.md:21)
4. **Stage each action so it reads.** Each frame needs one subject, a mover crossing the frame rather than coming at the lens, the destination kept in frame, and big poses held for several frames. (brick-toy STYLE.md:45,93; lowpoly-island DEMO.md:27; isometric-picture-book STYLE.md:12)
5. **Use arrival curves instead of popping things in.** Rise is a 0.5 s ease plus `sin(13s)e^(−7s)·0.18`; pop is `1−e^(−9s)cos(17s)`; landing squash is `1−0.16e^(−12s)cos(26s)` with volume preserved. Set the event time to the moment the object settles. (lowpoly-island DEMO.md:53)
6. **Step the characters but keep the camera smooth.** Characters and face textures animate at 12 fps (on twos); camera, focus and light run at the full frame rate. Use a two-frame idle at about 1.4 Hz and a blink every 3 s. Your 32×32 faces fit this hd-2d sprite approach directly. (brick-toy STYLE.md:43; hd-2d DEMO.md:64; brick-toy `main.js:65`)
7. **Use bevels and a slight sheen instead of raw boxes.** Bevel radius about 0.045–0.06 of a unit; roughness about 0.17–0.3 with a light clearcoat on characters; keep big ground surfaces matte. (brick-toy STYLE.md:18-19). If you keep the flat PS1 shading, follow lowpoly-island instead: flat shading, roughness 0.9, ±4% lightness jitter per piece.
8. **Use depth of field scaled to shot size, focused on the head.** The demos use a lens around 25–50 mm (fov 24–46). Most blur on close-ups, least on wides, so the hero never goes soft. (brick-toy DEMO.md:28; `main.js:129-169`)
9. **Apply one consistent grade.** Contrast about +0.26, saturation ×1.05–1.1, vignette 0.36–0.62, Neutral or ACES tone mapping, 2× supersampling against shimmer, light bloom (about 0.15–0.3, threshold ≥0.85). Use no grain on flat-colour or pixel looks. (brick-toy `main.js:13-21`; hd-2d DEMO.md:58; lowpoly-island STYLE.md:73)
10. **Keep colour disciplined.**
    - Saturated colour only on characters and hero objects, against a muted set.
    - One accent colour used only where the explanation is.
    - The hero in a colour no set uses.
    - Shadows tinted warm or purple, never grey.
    - Colours clustered by area, with large calm areas left empty.

    (brick-toy STYLE.md:29-30; isometric-picture-book STYLE.md:30-32; hd-2d STYLE.md:28; memphis-diorama STYLE.md:19,32)

**Text and audio to go with these:** hold subtitles at least max(1.8 s, speech + 0.6 s). Bring the key word in character by character, about 55–140 ms apart. Cut the music to silence right before the payoff beat.
